relevant_reference_lines: Input any exact equality system $Ax=b$ with $x\ge0$, including a rank-deficient raw system. Let $D$ be diagonal with $D_{ii}=-1$ when $b_i<0$ and $D_{ii}=1$ otherwise; set $\widetilde A=DA$ and $\widetilde b=Db\ge0$. Add artificial variables $u\in\mathbb R^m$ and solve the Phase I problem $\min\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u$ subject to $\widetilde A x+u=\widetilde b$, $x,u\ge0$, starting at $x=0,u=\widetilde b$ with artificial basis $I_m$. Use the exact primal algorithm of [[alg-revised-primal-simplex-bland-rule]] and its finite-termination result [[thm-revised-simplex-bland-rule-finite-termination]].

relevant_reference_lines: For any exact system $Ax=b$, $x\ge0$, the Phase I procedure of [[alg-revised-simplex-phase-one]] terminates. Its minimum artificial-variable sum is zero if and only if the original system is feasible. If the minimum is positive, its returned vector yields a Farkas infeasibility certificate, as defined in [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]], with $A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0$ and $b^{\mathsf T}q<0$. If the minimum is zero, the extraction procedure returns an equivalent full-row-rank reduced system with a basic feasible solution using only original columns; zero-valued artificial basic variables are either pivoted out or their redundant equations are removed.

[F1] [[alg-revised-simplex-phase-one]]: Phase I row-signs the equations, uses $[DA\ I]$ with initial $x=0,u=Db$, minimizes $\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u$, and extracts zero artificial basics by pivots or zero-row deletion.

[F2] [[thm-revised-simplex-bland-rule-finite-termination]]: Under its exact-arithmetic, finite-standard-form, full-row-rank hypotheses, the primal run terminates at an optimal basis or returns a strictly negative-cost feasible ray.
[F5] [[thm-farkas-alternative-for-finite-linear-systems]]: Exactly one of $x\ge0,Ax=b$ and existence of $q$ with $A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0,b^{\mathsf T}q<0$ holds for every finite real $A,b$.
